text:
elaine: opened a tiny docs PR to add a minimal reserved-pool example, a canary note for scale policies, and a short scale-down grace rationale. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4987

aj: nice. can you include a Go SDK snippet? most infra folks copy Go into their operator.

elaine: yeah, good call. sketching one now. also added a one-line note about canary routing to avoid overcommitting during rollout.

elaine: ```go
package main
import (
  "fmt"
  "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk"
)
func main() {
  client := redwood.NewDedicatedClient("$REDWOOD_KEY")
  resp, _ := client.CreateReservedPool(redwood.CreatePoolRequest{
    TenantID: "acme-tenant",
    GPUType:  "a100-40gb",
    MinReplicas: 2,
    MaxReplicas: 8,
    Isolation: "tenant_level",
    Autoscale: &redwood.AutoscaleConfig{CooldownSeconds: 240, ScaleUpThreshold: 0.75, GracePeriodSeconds: 300},
  })
  fmt.Println(resp.ID)
}
```

sam: small API naming nit: use `MinReplicas`/`MaxReplicas` in examples and call out mapping to `instances` in the backend. Also `Isolation` -> `tenant_level` as shown.

elaine: adjusted. added a sentence: "the SDK fields map to backend concepts; e.g., replicas -> instances."

michael: regarding the scale-down grace: please clarify why it's 300s in the example. otherwise customers will copy blindly. Suggest: "grace period reduces thrash for bursty traffic; tune to workload window."

elaine: added a rationale blurb under the YAML and SDK examples.

prashant: link hygiene: the PR references an old handbook path for "canary routing". new location is /docs/ops/traffic-management/canary-routing.html. can we update that?

elaine: fixed the link.

aj: docs smoke test failed earlier on markdownlint for the YAML snippet indentation. can you run the docs CI or fix inline?

docs-bot: CI run started (https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/43876).

elaine: fixed indentation and added an inline tf snippet per ask from infra engineers:
```hcl
resource "redwood_reserved_pool" "acme" {
  tenant = "acme-tenant"
  gpu_type = "a100-40gb"
  min_replicas = 2
  max_replicas = 8
  isolation = "tenant_level"
}
```

aj: perfect. one more doc UX ask: under "autoscale policy" section, can we surface a recommended default cooldown/grace pair for interactive workloads vs batch? like a small table or one-liner.

elaine: added a compact recommendations callout: "interactive: cooldown 120, grace 180; batch: cooldown 300, grace 600 (start conservative; measure)."

sam: good. also add a troubleshooting bullet under "Provisioning failures" : common cause: tenant label mismatch between TF and control plane.

elaine: added troubleshooting note and added a sample `redwood tenant list` command.

michael: SLA wording: current draft says "best-effort warm start" which Support flagged. Could we instead say: "Warm starts are attempted when capacity is available; cold starts may add 2-10s depending on model and instance type". keep it conservative.

elaine: updated wording to match that phrasing and added a cross-link to the SLA section in the dedicated docs.

prashant: optional: include a short note about tenant affinity and prewarm schedules for predictable diurnal loads. customers in AdTech asked.

elaine: added a 1-paragraph note and a sample cron-based prewarm snippet for dedicated.

elaine: also added a changelog bullet in the dedicated docs release notes: "added reserved-pool examples (Go/HCL), scale policy guidance, and troubleshooting notes".

docs-bot: CI passed (https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/43876). smoke tests green.

sam: lgtm. will do a quick pass to unify naming across other dedicated docs pages and then merge.

aj: please follow up with a tiny community post in #announcements when merged so customers spot the new examples.

elaine: will do. tagging support@ and infra@ for awareness. thanks all :rocket:
